answer: When one fraud signal fires in an epoch, every identity sharing correlated behaviour is slashed together: a single detected cheat burns the whole group's collateral, and the loss sends a ripple across all clones at once rather than punishing one head at a time. A lone ember of fraud therefore ignites the entire cluster's stake, so a sybil operator cannot isolate risk — each extra head raises the chance that one detection wipes everything, making expected cost grow faster than n while one honest identity risks nothing.
